title: test(objectql): bulk-write-per-row-hooks runs under the 10 s budget (#23182 row 5)
body:
Part of #23182 (row 5)

Row 5 of the test-budget card: `packages/objectql/src/bulk-write-per-row-hooks.test.ts`, project `local`, 16.1 s in the hourly battery's reading (run 38325245250). This PR is that file's fix and nothing else; the card stays open for its other rows. Test-only: one file, +37 / -15, no production file, no changeset (`skip-changeset` applied).

## Where the time went (measured, not guessed)

The file's test bodies cost 3.1 to 4.0 s on a quiet local box, and the module line is the number the budget reads. Instrumenting `seedTasks` inside the real file gave, in file order, 453, 392, 636, 585 and 687 ms for the five calls that push 10 001 (or 10 000) rows through `engine.insert`: 2.75 s of 3.69 s, about 74 percent. Those five calls belong to the ceiling cases (section 4 and D6). The last three are slower than the first two as the heap climbs from 481 to 604 MB across them. The remaining cost is the case that admits a batch exactly at the ceiling (about 0.5 to 0.7 s: 10 000 rows, so 20 000 real per-row hook dispatches) and about 0.25 s for the other 58 cases. There is no sleep, no timer, no wait and no per-test kernel boot in this file; the cost is row volume through `engine.insert`.

## What changed

The ceiling is judged on what the driver's `find` returns, so how those rows got into the stub store is not what the five cases pin. The stub driver gains a synchronous `seed(object, rows)` that stores the very rows `create()` stores (`create` and `seed` now share one `put`), and a helper `seedCeilingRows(driver, count, status)` lays down the matched set. The five ceiling cases seed through it instead of `engine.insert`. Every other seed in the file (2 to 4 rows) still goes through `engine.insert`.

Why the rows are the same ones: the engine adds nothing to a row on insert (a two-row probe gave `{title, status, id}` from `engine.insert` and from the driver alike). One-off check, not committed: for 10 001 `todo` rows, 10 000 `todo` rows and 10 001 `stale` rows, `driver.find` after `engine.insert` and after `seedCeilingRows` returned deep-equal arrays, and `engine.count` read the same total.

## Before / after, wall of the file (module line, default reporter, file alone, `--maxWorkers=2`, shared box, three runs each)

| reading | base file | this branch |
|:--|:--|:--|
| re-taken after a container restart, head eb84ae2f62 | 3149 / 3368 / 3426 ms | 963 / 871 / 837 ms |
| before the restart | 3987 / 3905 / 3598 ms (and 3635 ms in a one-off) | 962 / 971 / 940 ms |
| CI-shaped package run, before the restart: whole `local` project, 429 files, `--maxWorkers=8` on 4 cores, the base file copied under a temporary name into the same run | 8212 ms | 1780 ms |

Same 59 tests, same titles, same order. Slowest case after: "ADMITS a batch exactly AT the ceiling, in both phases", 682 ms (its 20 000 dispatches are the behaviour it pins, so it cannot shrink without weakening the pin); the next slowest is 50 ms. The card's 16.1 s was the slowest of 20 CI runs, about 4.4 times this box's 3.6 s reading; the same ratio puts this branch near 4 s in CI. That is a projection, not a measurement: NOT MEASURED until the next refresh PR's list is read. The single-file run's own `Duration` line (12 to 17 s) is dominated by the cold import and transform phase (about 11 s), which is on no module line, the same shape rows 1 and 4 noted.

## Pins preserved

No test deleted, no `.skip` / `.todo`, no timeout touched (the `60_000` on the at-ceiling case is unchanged), no project change, every assertion and every row count unchanged (10 001 and 10 000 still come from `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS`). Per-row hooks on bulk writes are still proven per row: the before and after hook counts at the ceiling are still asserted at 10 000 each.

## Ablation (on-disk proof via `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, wrap mode, restore proven: blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty)

Each leg ran the branch file and a temporary copy of the base file in one vitest invocation under the same mutation, and compared red sets by full test name.

| leg | mutation | base file red | branch file red | red sets |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| control | none | 0 / 59 | 0 / 59 | identical |
| A | `engine.ts` ceiling check never refuses (`if (verdict.kind) return;`) | 3 / 59 | 3 / 59 | identical: the section 4 refusal, the D6 before-update refusal, the D6 before-delete refusal |
| B | `engine.ts` ceiling check also refuses at the ceiling (a guard that refuses once `matched` reaches the limit) | 1 / 59 | 1 / 59 | identical: the at-ceiling admit case |
| C | `engine.ts` predicate-update before-hooks never dispatched (`rows.length > 99999999`) | 13 / 59 | 13 / 59 | identical |
| D | the new helper seeds one row short (`count - 1`) | n/a | 5 / 59 | the five ceiling cases, so none of them is satisfied by an empty or short set |

The subject (`engine.ts`) is imported by relative source path, so there is no dist leg; the mutation reached disk (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed) and every restore was verified.

## Verification (head eb84ae2f62)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: exit 0, including `check:test-typecheck` (39 files / 233 errors / 64 pinned signatures, unchanged; 0 errors in this file; the file is in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program, which is the one that covers it, and not in the default `tsconfig.json` program). Re-taken after the final edit.
- eslint `--no-inline-config` on the changed file: 0 errors, 0 warnings (1 file).
- Whole `local` project of the package, before the restart, on this change: 429 files / 8222 tests passed (that count includes the temporary base copy of this file).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 53 derived, 53 run, all exit 0; `--ran` reconciliation: 53 derived, 53 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. Beyond that, the 11 declared wide-population families and the 52 further artifact-roster families (one of the 53 roster entries is also in the commands list): 63 commands run, 59 exit 0. Four roster gates need a pull-request or workflow-event context and exited non-zero with their own "NOT MEASURED / NOT WIRED, no PR context" text, so they judged nothing in that run: `check-closing-target-claim`, `check-partof-closing-keyword`, `check-single-claim-paths`, `pm/check-governed-queue-guard`. `check-partof-closing-keyword` was then run on this body's own text (`PR_BODY` set): exit 0. The other three stay NOT MEASURED locally; CI supplies their context. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` first exited 3 (no dist); after a full workspace build (75 of 75 tasks) both exited 0.

## Acceptance notes

- The `60_000` timeout on the at-ceiling case could now be lowered; it is left alone on purpose (the card forbids touching timeouts, and a lowered one is a separate decision).
- `engine.insert` costs about 40 microseconds a row on a batch of 10 000 (about 0.4 s), growing as the heap fills. That is production cost, an optimisation and not a defect, so no card.
- The pin for this row is the next refresh PR's list no longer naming the file; that read is not available yet.
